evidence.summary: | Glenfarclas 1965/2005 (48.5%, Scott’s Selection) | Glenfarclas 1965/2005 (48.5%, Scott’s Selection)Four starsHere we have an old independently bottled Glenfarclas of approximately forty years of age. In short, a youngster… Colour: gold. Nose: waxes, hessian, mandarin peel, peach and apple skins, then a few touches of fennel and wormwood. Quite understated, very elegant, a little reserved, but this resistance to modernity can only be charming. Others would immediately have subjected it to some more or less brutal re-racking. Mouth: refined, admittedly a little bitter and herbaceous, but it all works, even if it tends to dive towards… the turf, almost like a rugby player. Finish: there are some lovely aspects, but overall it’s a little short on fruit. Comments: perhaps this lovely cask had already crossed the ‘maturity pass’ two or four years earlier. But it’s still very beautiful, of course. SGP:361 - 85 points. |

Scott's Selection is the independent label on this Glenfarclas 1965, bottled in 2005 at 48.5%. Spink's original auction catalog names Robert Scott & Co. as the bottling business. Just Whisky independently records Scott's Selection and the same vintage, bottling year and strength. Approximately forty years is not a printed age statement.

The source reviews one Glenfarclas 1979/2014 official Family Casks bottling for The Bow Bar and Shinanoya. The matching exact catalog entry confirms cask 8801, 50.8% ABV, 212 bottles, and a 2014 bottling date. The 212 is the release outturn. The original retailer Shinanoya describes GLENFARCLAS [1979-2014] PLAIN HOGSHEAD #8801 for THE BOW BAR & Shinanoya as an official distillery-bottled selection.

The producer announces Glenfarclas 190 as a 2026 anniversary release at 51.4% ABV, explicitly equivalent to 90 British proof. The source review gives a total of 15,000 bottles. This is one marketed whisky, not a pack of bottles. Luvians, an independent specialist retailer, records the exact Glenfarclas 190th Anniversary release at 51.4% with Bottles Produced: 15,000 and bottling date 2026.
